test.description: Mode A for William Ashford (b. ~1838 Canterbury, Kent, England; d. 1874), resident only in England. timeline_build reads census years from its census table, so the person timeline expects the English censuses of 1841, 1861 and 1871 (1851 is documented) and no US federal year.

judge_context: The delegation names a person and no timeline or hypothesis, so it is Mode A: the agent calls `timeline_build`, which writes the person timeline `t_001` (the project had none). The `person-timeline-in-code` validator owns the call. Grade `t_001`.
`t_001` holds four events, all at Canterbury, Kent, England: birth ~1838, the 1851 census residence, the 1859 marriage and the 1874 death.

Its gaps: `high` ~1838 to 1851 naming the 1841 England and Wales census; `high` 1859 to 1874 naming the 1861 and 1871 England and Wales censuses; `medium` burial at 1874. No US federal census year (1850, 1860, 1870, ...) may appear for this England-only life.
Census years in Mode A come from `timeline_build`'s census table, never from the wiki: the agent makes no `wiki_read` call and none is expected.

In Mode A `timeline_build` resolves every place and computes every `distance_from_previous_km` itself, in code, so the agent makes no `place_search` or `place_distance` call for the person timeline and none is expected. Do not mark Tool usage or Tool Arguments down for their absence, and do not ask a persisted `standard_place` or distance to trace to a call the agent made: they are the tool's. A place or distance the reply states must match the persisted timeline. `distance_from_previous_km` is the distance from the immediately preceding event in the sorted list, and `null` where either place has no coordinates.
The distance dimension is N/A: all events are at the same place (Canterbury), so there is no distance-sensitive pair to judge.
